space: Haima seep core QDN-14B and non-seep core QDN-31B, northwestern South China Sea.
time: Cross-sectional piston-core comparison; collection date not specified in the inspected abstract.
design: Two piston cores compared using geochemical profiles, archaeal 16S rRNA genes, and mcrA phylogeny.
finding: ANME lineages occupied different sediment niches: ANME-2a/b predominated in upper and middle sulfate–methane transition layers, whereas ANME-1b was more prominent in deeper sulfate-depleted layers.
limit: Two cores describe local zonation; marker-gene occurrence does not identify electron-transfer mechanisms.

space: GMGS2-08, northern South China Sea, including present and buried seep systems.
time: GMGS2 expedition cores; collection timing not specified in the inspected abstract.
design: qPCR and 16S rRNA sequencing compared sulfate–methane transition, carbonate, and upper/lower hydrate-bearing zones.
finding: Microbial assemblages differed among hydrate-bearing, transition, and carbonate zones; ANME-1b occurred prominently in hydrate-bearing intervals.
limit: Taxonomic patterns support habitat differentiation, while the proposed AOM roles remain inferred.

space: Water above two South China Sea cold seeps.
time: Cross-sectional vertical profiles; sampling dates not specified in the inspected abstract.
design: Particle-attached and free-living fractions analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and qPCR along vertical geochemical gradients.
finding: Particle-attached and free-living prokaryotic fractions differed in abundance and diversity; free-living communities were more associated with temperature and inorganic nutrients.
limit: Fractions are operationally defined; amplicons do not quantify methane oxidation or organic-carbon turnover rates.

space: Newly developed ROV05 and ROV07 seeps, northern South China Sea.
design: ROV cores and surface samples across living clams, dead shells, and carbonate habitats; paired DNA/RNA amplicons, qPCR, and geochemistry.
finding: DNA- and RNA-derived assemblages differed, with RNA libraries showing stronger representation of methane-cycling archaea and sulfate reducers in particular seep habitats.
limit: RNA enrichment is an activity indicator, not a direct measurement of AOM rate; the associated corrigendum should accompany citation.

space: Eight cores from two South China Sea seep areas, including three shallow-SMTZ cores.
time: Cross-sectional sediment-depth comparison; dates not specified in the inspected abstract.
design: Genome reconstruction and transcript evidence used to characterize sulfur-oxidizing and sulfur-reducing populations above and below SMTZ.
finding: The 110 recovered sulfur-cycling genomes supported distinct niches above and below SMTZ, linking inferred sulfur metabolism with carbon fixation and nitrogen fixation.
limit: Genomic pathways and transcripts do not directly determine electron budgets or in situ process rates.

space: Haima non-seep, low-intensity, and high-intensity sites; water approximately 50 cm above seabed.
design: ROV-mounted Niskin bottles; 4 L filtered through 0.22 µm membranes; 16S sequencing compared with methane, nutrients, and DOC.
finding: Bottom-water bacterial composition differed among seep-intensity regimes; the high-intensity site had the lowest alpha diversity and methane was associated with community variation.
limit: One expedition and correlative community analyses do not establish hydrocarbon degradation rates.
locator: Abstract; Collection of Bottom-Water Samples and Geochemical Analysis

space: Site F waters, seep fluids, fluids beneath fauna, and sediment cores.
design: 23 metagenomes; near-fauna water collected by ROV and filtered through 0.22 µm membranes, with depth-sectioned sediment cores.
finding: The study supplied 768 MAGs from Site F samples, including 597 bacterial and 171 archaeal genomes, expanding genomic references across seep compartments.
limit: MAGs ranged in completeness; the number is a recovered-genome count, not a count of viable species.

space: Eleven sediment cores from two geographically separated South China Sea seeps.
time: Cross-sectional comparison across high-, low-, and non-seep methane regimes.
design: Geochemical and microbiological profiles; assembly models and co-occurrence networks compared across methane-supply classes.
finding: Communities grouped by methane-supply regime across sites, with ANME-1 more prominent under high supply and ANME-2 under low supply.
limit: Supply classes and network models do not prove causal interactions between individual taxa.

space: Qiongdongnan Basin and Shenhu hydrate sediments; analyzed samples to 49 m below seabed.
design: Four drill cores, geochemical zonation, MAGs, and metatranscriptomes compared above and below sulfate–methane interfaces.
finding: Abundant populations carried and expressed macromolecule-fermentation pathways, while classical sulfate reducers, methanogens, and methanotrophs were comparatively rare.
limit: Transcription supports metabolic engagement but does not quantify the energy contribution of fermentation for the entire sediment column.

space: Six global seep sites, including Haima, Site F, and Haiyang 4; sediments to 430 cm.
time: Compiled datasets from multiple campaigns; not a synchronous global survey.
design: Microdiversity and selection analysis for 39 abundant methane-oxidizing and sulfate-reducing species from 68 metagenomes.
finding: Population genomes showed generally low homologous recombination and strong purifying selection, with sediment-depth-dependent diversification of key metabolic genes.
limit: Global aggregate results must be distinguished from SCS-specific populations; sampling and read coverage affect microdiversity recovery.
locator: Abstract; Methods: Metagenomes for deep-sea cold seep sediments

space: Haima core HM-S11; methanic sediments beneath the sulfate-rich zone.
design: Porewater/solid geochemistry, DNA/RNA communities, metagenomes, metatranscriptomes, and modeling examined Fe/Mn-linked AOM.
finding: Geochemical, omics, and model evidence supported an additional methane sink linked to iron and manganese reduction in methanic sediments.
limit: The pathway contribution is model-estimated; it does not experimentally confirm a specific metal-reducing partner.

space: Nine stations in Haima, Site F, and Xisha Trough; 0–4 cm surface sediments.
design: Surface sediments were examined with geochemistry and 13CH4 slurry incubations under sulfate, nitrate, and nitrite amendments.
finding: The study provided incubation evidence for nitrate/nitrite-dependent methane oxidation in addition to sulfate-associated pathways in SCS seep sediments.
limit: Incubation potentials are not equivalent to unamended in situ rates or region-wide pathway fractions.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and chemical analysis; Measurement of AOM rates

type: Cultivation plus in situ functional study
space: Formosa cold seep, seawater–sediment interface and reduced sediment.
time: KEXUE cruises in 2020 and 2021; 14-day in situ water incubation.
design: Sulfurovum/Sulfurimonas isolates integrated with comparative genomes, transcripts, geochemistry, and gas-tight in situ sampling.
finding: Culture and transcript evidence linked Campylobacterota to hydrogen utilization, sulfur transformations, and nitrate consumption at the seep interface.
limit: Functions of cultured representatives and expressed pathways should not be assigned uniformly to all Campylobacterota.

space: Two active and one extinct Haima seep site; upper 18–20 cm sediments.
time: Cross-sectional seep-stage comparison from 16 sediment metagenomes.
design: Viral genomes, predicted hosts, defense systems, and population nucleotide diversity recovered from bulk sediment metagenomes.
finding: The study recovered 338 vOTUs and identified candidate viral persistence strategies alongside low within-population nucleotide diversity.
limit: Host links and auxiliary functions are computational predictions; sequence recovery does not demonstrate active infection.
locator: Abstract; Sample description, metagenomic sequencing and analysis

type: Fungal community networks and gene-expression analysis
space: Haima seep/control sediments plus comparative datasets from ten global seep regions.
time: Compiled community and omics datasets; not a repeated-rate experiment.
design: 147-sample fungal/prokaryotic networks integrated with metagenomic and metatranscriptomic searches for fungal enzymes.
finding: Fungal sequences occupied connected network positions and fungal genes were transcribed in seep sediments, supporting inclusion of fungi in seep-microbiome studies.
limit: Network centrality and fungal transcripts do not demonstrate direct fungal methane oxidation or causal ecosystem control.
locator: Abstract; Environmental context of cold seep and control samples

space: Haima seep and non-seep stations; water 160–200 m above seabed and 0–6 cm sediments.
design: CTD-rosette water samples and gravity-core surface sediments compared using community and elemental analyses.
finding: Seep and reference samples differed in elemental distribution and bacterial network structure; water and sediment assemblages were more similar at seepage stations.
limit: These water samples were not taken immediately at the interface; network association does not prove sediment-to-water migration of cells.

space: Vertical water profile above Haima cold seep.
time: Cross-sectional water-column survey; collection dates not retained in the inspected abstract.
design: Depth-stratified communities compared with hydrochemistry and statistical assembly/co-occurrence models.
finding: Prokaryotic diversity and modeled assembly processes changed with depth and hydrochemistry, with Cyanobacteria prominent near the illuminated surface and Proteobacteria deeper.
limit: Statistical assembly classifications depend on null-model assumptions and cannot directly measure microbial interactions.

space: Seven interface-water samples from Site F and Lingshui seeps.
design: ROV-collected interface water and 16S amplicons compared across seepage and fauna habitats.
finding: Interface microbiomes differed between Lingshui and Site F, with distinct inferred methane-, nitrogen-, and sulfur-associated functional profiles.
limit: Function predictions from marker genes do not establish the rates or realized occurrence of individual AOM pathways.
locator: Abstract; Samples collection and geochemistry measurement

space: Haima active-seep and reference-area sediment cores.
time: Cross-sectional comparison; collection date not specified in inspected publisher abstract.
design: Hg/MeHg concentrations and mercury isotopes integrated with microbial hgcA, merA, and merB gene analyses.
finding: Upper active-seep sediments contained more Hg and methylmercury than reference sediments, alongside genes associated with mercury transformations.
limit: Gene detection does not measure methylation rate; the paper's global storage extrapolation is not a direct global inventory.

type: Field and in situ nutrient-enrichment experiment
space: Water column above Haima cold seep.
time: Field observations and in situ incubations; sampling chronology not specified in inspected abstract.
design: Nitrogen-fixation rates, nifH communities, DOM amendments, and MAGs used to examine sulfur-associated diazotrophy.
finding: Nitrogen fixation occurred in Haima water and increased following sulfur-containing organic-matter enrichment; Dechloromonas genomes carried nitrogen-fixation and sulfur-oxidation genes.
limit: Amendment responses measure experimental potential; co-encoded genes do not independently establish sulfur oxidation as the in situ energy source.

space: Haima seep, less-active seep, and non-seep sediments.
design: ROV sediment cores; paired DNA/RNA profiling for prokaryotes and microeukaryotes with environmental and assembly analyses.
finding: Prokaryotes generally had lower diversity in seep sediments than reference sediments, whereas microeukaryotes showed the opposite pattern; DNA/RNA differences were larger for microeukaryotes.
limit: RNA signatures cannot be equated directly with biomass production or organism viability.
locator: Abstract; Sampling collection and measurement of environmental factors

space: Site F, roughly 1150 m water depth; surface, mesopelagic, and near-vent water.
design: ROV interface filtration and Niskin samples at 30–1100 m; 0.22 µm filters, MAG reconstruction, and metabolic models.
finding: The 377 MAGs supported vertical metabolic differentiation, including methanotrophic populations from bottom-interface water into deeper mesopelagic layers.
limit: Predicted exchanges and methane-filtration functions are genome/model inferences rather than measured methane removal fluxes.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection; The metabolic potential and interaction of water column microbes

space: Sixteen global seep sites, including Haima and Qiongdongnan samples.
time: Compiled datasets, with QDN-W07 sediments sampled in 2021 and 2023.
design: Protein-model classification integrated with genomes, transcripts, porewater chemistry, metabolomics, and enzyme validation.
finding: LucaPCycle expanded phosphorus-cycling protein detection, revealing archaeal and viral genetic potential and validating selected previously unannotated phosphatases.
limit: Global protein-family totals are not SCS-specific counts; annotations do not establish phosphorus flux for every host.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets and processing

space: Sixteen global seep sites, including Haima, Site F, Shenhu, and other SCS sites.
design: RdhA-like sequence classification integrated with halogen chemistry, laboratory incubations, transcripts, and metabolomics.
finding: Reductive-dehalogenase-like genes occurred across diverse archaeal and bacterial groups, with complementary chemical and experimental evidence supporting organohalide-transforming potential.
limit: RdhA-like annotation alone does not verify substrate specificity or field-scale remediation capacity.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets from cold seep sediments

space: Seventeen global seep sites including Haima, Site F, and other SCS regions.
design: Quorum-sensing genes and transcripts compared with environmental gradients; representative LuxI–LuxR pairs tested by heterologous expression.
finding: Multiple signaling systems were detected across seep taxa, and representative LuxI–LuxR pairs showed activity in heterologous tests.
limit: Presence and experimental function of selected signaling pairs do not demonstrate regulation of every inferred biogeochemical pathway in situ.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data processing

space: Site F sponge-associated, seawater, and sediment microbiomes.
time: Sponge samples from 2021 compared with environmental samples from 2017.
design: Six sponge species and environmental metagenomes compared using taxonomic profiles, MAGs, and functional annotations.
finding: Sponge microbiomes had distinct composition, lower diversity, and enrichment of specialized sulfur- and methane-associated bacterial groups compared with environmental microbiomes.
limit: Different collection years confound direct habitat comparisons; functional gene abundance is not metabolic efficiency.

space: Seventeen global seep sites; SCS sequences contribute to the comparative catalog.
design: Microbial defense and viral anti-defense genes compared across genomes; selected candidate defenses experimentally tested.
finding: The comparative catalog revealed extensive defense and anti-defense diversity, and selected candidate microbial systems protected against viral infection in laboratory assays.
limit: Laboratory validation covers selected systems; co-occurrence does not establish synergism or infection rates in seep sediment.

space: Site F, near-seep sites and a station approximately 1 km away.
design: Niskin bottles on CTD and ROV; 16S and metagenomic profiles compared across depth and distance.
finding: Near-seep and deeper-water communities showed greater representation of methane- and sulfur-associated populations and genes, indicating spatially structured metabolic potential.
limit: Gene distributions do not quantify the fraction of vented methane removed during upward transport.
locator: Abstract; Water Samples Collection and Pretreatment

space: Haima water layers and mussel, anemone, bare seabed, dead-clam, and clam sediment habitats.
design: CTD water profiles and ROV sediment cores to 30 cm; prokaryotic/microeukaryotic community and co-occurrence analyses.
finding: Microbial diversity and co-occurrence varied by compartment and habitat; modeled environmental selection differed between prokaryotes and microeukaryotes in water versus sediment.
limit: Correlations and assembly models indicate ecological patterns, not demonstrated interspecies exchanges.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and measurement of environmental factors

space: Early-stage and mature South China Sea seep sediments.
time: Cross-stage comparison with geochemistry, labeling, and incubation experiments.
design: 14C labeling, omics, and gas-production analyses tested nitrate/nitrite-linked methane oxidation and N2O formation.
finding: Nitrate/nitrite-coupled methane oxidation had a larger potential contribution in early-stage than mature seep sediments, and nitrate/methane amendments increased net N2O production.
limit: Potential rates and amendment responses cannot be treated as continuous natural emissions or global climate offsets.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and geochemical analysis

type: Multi-year in situ seep succession study
space: Human-induced newborn SCS seep compared with mature seeps and slope references.
design: More than 40 sites around the discharge center; ROV cores, porewater, molecular analyses, and in situ ecosystem observations.
finding: A methane-consuming animal–microbe assemblage developed within approximately one to two years at the monitored newborn seep, with aerobic and anaerobic methanotrophs and bioturbating fauna.
limit: One induced seep does not establish a universal recovery time or guaranteed mitigation of future methane releases.

space: Haima sediment core at 1435 m water depth; four depth intervals within 30 cm.
design: Long-read reconstruction of circular MAGs, genomic-hotspot comparisons, and heterologous tests of hicAB operons.
finding: ANME-1 genomes contained variable hotspots associated with defense, transport, and methane-metabolism genes; heterologous hicAB tests supported toxin–antitoxin function.
limit: One core and heterologous assays do not prove the drivers of speciation or stress responses in natural ANME populations.
locator: Abstract; Sampling, DNA extraction, metagenomic library preparations and sequencing

space: Archivesica marissinica and sulfur-oxidizing symbionts at Haima, including HM-2 and HM-3.
time: Experimental comparison across sulfide-availability treatments; publication 2 October 2026.
design: In situ clam transplantation with host/symbiont molecular profiling under moderate and severe sulfide shortage.
finding: Moderate sulfide shortage preserved symbiont abundance, whereas severe shortage coincided with reduced abundance and altered host lysosomal pathways; sulfur-metabolism responses indicated symbiotic flexibility.
limit: Molecular associations support a proposed buffering mechanism but do not directly measure symbiont carbon transfer or long-term resilience.

space: Six sponge species at the Formosa Ridge cold seep.
design: Sixteen sponge samples analyzed with full-length 16S amplicons and bacterial phylogeny.
finding: The six sponge species hosted distinct bacterial assemblages, with SUP05 prominent in most samples.
limit: Marker phylogeny does not measure sulfur/methane oxidation or establish the mechanism of host specificity.
locator: Abstract; 2.1 Sample collection; 2.3 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and processing
